short_description: AI chat that works offline on your phone, with optional cloud.
full_description:
AGI is an AI assistant that runs on your phone first.

LOCAL MODE
• Chat with an on-device model, even offline or in airplane mode
• No account needed; local chats stay on this device, encrypted at rest
• The default model downloads once and runs locally after that

AGI CLOUD (optional, sign-in)
• Cloud chat and web search on the Free plan
• Projects, memory and skills on the Free plan
• The app is free and has no in-app purchases

PRIVACY
• Cloud messages go to the AI provider that serves the request
• Limit which AI providers may be used in Settings > Privacy
• Export or delete your data any time in Settings
• India DPDP notice and open items: https://agiworkforce.com/trust

Built by AGI Automation LLC, USA.
Support: support@agiworkforce.com
Privacy: https://agiworkforce.com/privacy
Terms: https://agiworkforce.com/terms

content_rating.iarc_rating: Teen (expected), with Diverse Content: Discretion Advised
content_rating.note: A rating of the content only, assigned by IARC from the questionnaire; it is not the eligibility rule, which is target_audience (18 and over). Mirrors ChatGPT and Claude on Google Play (both Teen, Diverse Content: Discretion Advised, checked 2026-10-19). AI output is not fixed content, so answer the IARC questions for the most mature output the filters allow, not the median reply. Unrestricted internet access is true: a link in an answer opens any http or https page in an in-app Custom Tab (openUntrustedUrlInAppBrowser in apps/mobile/lib/safeOpenURL.ts, called from apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MarkdownInline.tsx), and Cloud chats run web search. user_generated_content_shared is true for projects and agents shared by people the user works with and for artifacts a user publishes; in_app_communication_with_unknown_users is false because the app has no person-to-person messaging; shares_user_location is false because the app requests no location permission. Google's content rating pages read on 2026-11-15 (answers 9898843, 188189 and 9859655) do not show the questionnaire's wording, so these keys describe what each answer must reflect, not the live question text: read each question in Play Console before answering.

target_audience.play_console_state: Reported by the owner on 2026-11-20, not verified from the repository: Play Console App content, Target audience and content has "18 and over" as the only target age group, with Restrict Minor Access on. Internal-test build 6 still ships the earlier 13 and over gate; the production draft has release notes and no bundle attached.
target_audience.note: Since 2026-11-20 the app is for people 18 and over. 18 is the lowest age the binary admits: getAgeThreshold in apps/mobile/src/features/auth/services/ageGate.ts takes its default from ACCOUNT_MINIMUM_AGE (18, packages/contracts/types/src/account-eligibility.ts), and no regional row is lower (India and Brazil are 18). The age step comes before anything else on every path, account-free Local Mode included (src/features/auth/services/rootRouting.ts). It asks Play Age Signals for the 18 threshold where available and falls back to a typed age (src/features/age-assurance/ageAssurance.ts). A device that recorded an age under 18 is refused on every path and offered Sign out, Export this device's data, Erase this device's data and the web data-rights page; there is no minor-safe mode and no parental controls screen. This is who may use the app; the IARC rating under content_rating is a separate rating of the content and is not changed to express it.

data_collected_types.collected_when: Only when the user signs in to use AGI Cloud.
Only if provided by the user's sign-in method when signing in to AGI Cloud.

In AGI Cloud: the messages the user sends are uploaded to AGI Cloud and forwarded to the model provider serving the request. Local Mode chats are not uploaded. In Local Mode, only a content report the person chooses to send, which uploads the reported answer to AGI.
Only in AGI Cloud: photos attached to a message or set as the account avatar are uploaded.
Only in AGI Cloud: documents attached to a message are uploaded.

Only during live voice mode in an AGI Cloud chat: AGI Cloud sets up the call, then the audio streams directly between the device and the voice provider, and the transcript is saved to that chat. Dictation transcribes on the device and uploads no audio.
Only in AGI Cloud, when a chat asks about the user's schedule and calendar access is allowed: the events it reads, with titles, times, places and notes, go to AGI Cloud and the model provider.
Only in AGI Cloud: chat search queries are sent to AGI Cloud, recorded against the account, and sent to the embedding provider to rank results when the account has indexed content.
Only after sign-in: the account identifier carried by every authenticated cloud request.

On every install, signed in or not: the update check sends Expo's per-install client ID on every launch, and Google's ML Kit SDKs send per-installation identifiers when on-device text recognition, translation or the Android system model runs. While signed in to AGI Cloud: an app-generated install ID with the device name and OS version, sent on every active session to list the device in the account and registered with the push token when notifications are allowed. No advertising identifier is collected.

Only in AGI Cloud and only after the user allows product analytics in Settings, Privacy (off by default; a workspace administrator can also turn it off): event names such as a stopped or regenerated response, recorded against the account. No message, file or file name is included. Local Mode sends none.
Only in AGI Cloud: the support tickets and replies and the in-app feedback the user writes are stored against the account. In Local Mode, feedback opens the device mail app instead.

Google's ML Kit SDKs send device information, app information and performance metrics when on-device text recognition, translation or the Android system model runs, Local Mode included. A Cloud support ticket attaches app version, platform, device class, locale, time zone and screen size unless the user turns that off.
On every install, signed in or not: the update check sends Expo the last error that stopped the app from launching and the IDs of updates that failed to launch.

data_safety.note: Ground facts. Local Mode uploads no chat content: apps/mobile/lib/egressGuard.ts blocks AGI hosts while Local Mode is active, except a content report the person chooses to send and, for a signed-in account, the account and withdrawal controls, which send the account identifier and no chat content. Two SDKs send data in every mode: expo-updates asks Expo's update service for an update on every launch with a per-install client ID and launch errors, and on Android Google's ML Kit sends diagnostics and per-installation identifiers when its on-device features run. Signing in to AGI Cloud adds account email, optional name, account and device identifiers, the conversation content, attachments, calendar events and search queries the user sends, support tickets and feedback, and product interaction events only with the user's analytics consent. Sharing. Google defines sharing as a transfer to a third party and exempts a service provider that processes data on the developer's behalf (the service-provider exception, https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10787469). Messages, photos, files, voice, calendar events and search queries reach the model, voice or embedding provider serving the request, and on the Free plan some of those providers' terms allow training on what they receive, so the exception cannot be shown to apply and those types are answered shared. Clerk (sign-in), the push service, Expo (update checks) and Google ML Kit (diagnostics) receive data only to provide their service, so those types are answered not shared. Whether the model providers' terms make them service providers is for the owner and counsel; until they decide, shared is the answer. Optional. Types sent only after Cloud sign-in or by a feature the user chooses are optional. Device or other IDs, Diagnostics and Crash logs are required, because SDKs send them without sign-in and the app gives no control. Not every request goes to AGI: the device also contacts Clerk for sign-in, Expo for update checks, Google for ML Kit on Android, the push service, and in live voice the voice provider directly. apps/mobile/package.json declares no ad, analytics or crash-reporting SDK. store-listing/android/data-safety.json holds the same types with the same sharing and optionality answers, and REVIEWER-NOTES-ANDROID.md states the same.

in_app_products.note: Version 1 has no in-app products. apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json sets "nativePurchases": false, and src/features/billing/nativePurchaseAvailability.ts exports it as NATIVE_PURCHASES_AVAILABLE, which every purchase path reads. With it false the app shows no purchase, upgrade, top-up, restore-purchases, compare-plans or contact-sales control and no price; useMobileIap.ts picks an inert implementation at build time, so the app never opens a Play Billing connection; mobileIapService.ts refuses catalog and verify calls, so the app never calls /api/mobile/iap/*; and app.config.js removes the permission com.android.vending.BILLING from the manifest. The purchase client library expo-iap is still linked into the binary and its config plugin is still registered in app.config.js, but nothing calls it. On the server the /api/mobile/iap/* routes (owner mobile-iap-catalog.ts) stay off unless the deployment sets MOBILE_IAP_ENABLED. Do not activate Play products for this release. Settings > Subscription opens a screen titled Plan: current plan, renewal or end date if any, a plain-text Billing line ("Managed on the web", "By your organization", "Included with your account" or "Managed where you subscribed") for an account that already holds a paid plan, "What your plan includes", "Usage" and "Help with your plan", which opens in-app support. A feature outside the account's plan is described as not included in the plan, with no call to action. Paid plans exist for the web product, but nothing is sold on any platform before 1 January 2027: no plan or credit can be bought in the app, on the web or anywhere else, and the plans that exist were granted without a purchase. An account that holds one gets that plan's access after signing in, and the app neither sells nor advertises plans. The review account's plan was granted for review without a purchase, so its Plan screen shows "Included with your account"; the app has no purchase, upgrade or price. Selling in the app needs nativePurchases set to true, a new store build and a new review.

release_notes_v0_0_1:
AGI 0.0.1, first release.

• On-device AI chat works offline, no account needed
• Catalog-selected on-device model downloads once and runs locally
• Sign in to AGI Cloud for cloud chat, web search, projects, memory and skills on the Free plan
• No in-app purchases
• On-device voice transcription

Email support@agiworkforce.com, we read everything.
